rules: A $return-transformed leg failed cheap_screen regardless of its partner (5 of 8 fails this round): pure-return shapes (IF_ELSE on TS_SUM($return,3); BOUND+TS_STD($return)) and return+price mixes (TS_DECAY_LINEAR($return,10)-TS_MEAN($return,10) vs TS_RANK($open,21); TS_PRODUCT(1+$return,63) vs TS_ARGMIN($close,63); TS_SUM(POWER($return,2),10) vs TS_DELTA($close,63)) all failed. A price-side partner does not rescue a $return leg.

CS_RANK($roe) x CS_RANK(TS_RANK($dollar_volume,21) - X) works when X is a price/range stat (two accepts: X=TS_STD($open,10) at 3.462; TS_MAX($high,21) on the other side at 2.825) but is saturated when X involves $return - swapping TS_MEAN for TS_STD and the window on $return still hit rho 0.990 against an archived member. Keep exploring this template with price fields, not $return.

CS_RANK($high - $close) is now a claimed bolt-on leg: stacking it as a third rank term (with an EPS x TS_MIN($low,21) pair) still shared 4 nodes with the existing accept CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($open,5)/(TS_STD($open,63)+1e-8)) x CS_RANK($high-$close). Use it as one of exactly two multiplied legs, not three.

TS_RANK(price,60-90d) x TS_STD(volatility term) collapses to one signal even when fields AND windows differ on both sides: TS_RANK($close,90)/TS_STD($return,21) hit rho 0.817 against TS_RANK($open,63)/TS_STD($high/$low ratio,90). The crossing structure itself is claimed, not just the specific fields.

EPS x TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21) collapses to the same signal regardless of the third ingredient or connecting operator: a rank-spread adding a return-rank term (rho 0.867) collided with an archived product/ratio version built with $close instead. Don't expect a new third ingredient to decorrelate this pair.

In-run duplicates held at 30% (6/20). The one repeated family, EPS/price-ratio minus a return-stat (TS_MIN($low,21) denom with TS_STD(return); $close denom with TS_RANK(return)), is also the cross-run-saturated 'RANK(eps) minus RANK(X)' shape already in memory - the proposer is regenerating a globally stale pattern, not just repeating in-run.

Round's best fitness (7.285, hard-to-fill fast/price_volume/high niche) crossed a long-window TS_ARGMIN($low,126) against a 1-day TS_DELTA($high). Long-horizon extremum timing on one OHLC field vs. a 1-day delta on a different field is a promising, still-open shape worth extending to other field pairs and nearby short lags.

Fundamental/price ratio crossed with a second RAW fundamental rank scores well (CS_RANK($asset_turnover/$close) x CS_RANK($roe) = 6.902) but crossing two normalized ratios together is weak (CS_RANK($book_per_share/$dollar_volume) x CS_RANK($accrual_gap/$open) = |t| 0.14). Keep one side of these products a bare fundamental rank; don't normalize both legs.
